# The blueprint, thing by thing

Rendered from the declarations by `pnpm generate`: this page, and one page per thing beside it with each of its verbs'
promises (today's word in the code: claims). Do not edit them by hand: a test fails when a page and its sources differ.

Each claim is checked black-box by the journeys (`packages/scenarios`; docs/roadmap.md, "Scenarios are journeys"):
through the door, reading only what the operations answer and what the world's door shows of its chain. No claim has
a scenario of its own. Its operation's checks run on every call of that operation in every journey, and the journeys'
steps call it as the claim says; `packages/scenarios/src/coverage.ts` names, for each claim, the checks and the
steps. "In" names the starting world whose state a claim speaks of: a journey checks it in that state, whether it
starts from that world or starts earlier and brings its world there by its own steps. "Old" names the claim of the old
blueprint (`docs/thin-line/operations.json`, its `evalId`) it keeps, word for word or rewritten.

## What the runner checks on every call

These hold for every call of every journey, so no claim repeats them:

1. A successful call emits exactly the events its outcome declares, each once, each carrying exactly what the
   declaration computes from the call's payload and answer, and nothing more. A refused call emits none.
2. A refusal is one the operation declares.
3. The call's spans are recorded under the trace id the caller sent, the first named after the operation.
4. The call's time, as the caller saw it and as the server's span measured it, is stored with the run, with the
   time of each step beneath it, next to the operation's budget. A budget is recorded, not enforced: nothing fails
   on speed until a budget is set from measured runs.

## Starting worlds

Declared in `src/starting-points/points.ts`. Each is made through the door from the one before it, then either saved as a template that a journey starting from it gets (the runner's one world reset in place to it), or made by its steps for each journey. A journey reads the facts of its world, and of every world it is made from, with `given` (src/starting-points/facts.ts).

- `nothing`. The platform is deployed. No world has the name the journey uses. The journey's operator owns fewer live worlds than the limit, and a second operator exists. The facts name both operators. A journey from it gets it made by its steps. Facts it adds: `operators`, `calls`.
- `quota-full`. Made from `nothing`. The journey's operator owns as many live private worlds as one owner may have. Steps: `world.create` as operator: creates private worlds until the limit is reached (fact `filled`). A journey from it gets it made by its steps. Facts it adds: `filled`.
- `fresh`. Made from `nothing`. A private world owned by the journey's operator, its clock frozen. Its cast: dana, eli, sam and olga, each with a claimed personal Safe holding 10,000 USDC, and pat, who has not finished signing up and has no Safe. No company. Steps: `world.create` as operator: creates a private world with a frozen clock and a lifetime of 60 minutes (fact `world`). A journey from it gets it from its template. Facts it adds: `world`.
- `founded`. Made from `fresh`. Northwind (handle `northwind`), founded by dana: Directors dana and eli, 2 of 2; members sam and pat with no permission; 1,000 USDC of dana's capital in the company Safe; its site ready, with users for dana and eli. Steps: `org.create` as dana: founds northwind with eli as a Director, threshold 2, members sam and pat, and 1,000 USDC of capital (fact `founded`); `approval.sign` as dana: signs her setup approval (fact `setupCollected`); `approval.sign` as eli: signs his setup approval, which sends the setup (fact `setupSent`); wait as operator: until world.show lists northwind's site as ready. A journey from it gets it from its template. Facts it adds: `founded`, `setupCollected`, `setupSent`.
- `office-holder`. Made from `founded`. sam holds Manage books: his Safe wears the Books hat and he has a user on Northwind's site. The site holds no document yet. Steps: `org.member.grant` as dana: grants sam manage-books (fact `grant`); `approval.sign` as dana: signs the proposal (fact `grantCollected`); `approval.sign` as eli: signs the proposal, which executes it (fact `grantSent`); wait as sam: until report.run of the General Ledger stops refusing with NoSiteUser; a report makes nothing. A journey from it gets it from its template. Facts it adds: `grant`, `grantCollected`, `grantSent`.
- `payment-drafted`. Made from `office-holder`. The supplier Brightside Cleaning Ltd with a payment address; a submitted Purchase Invoice of 125.50 USDC from it; and a draft Payment Entry paying that invoice from the Capxul Safe account. Their fields are the vocabulary's (src/common/site.ts). Steps: `doc.create` as sam: creates the Supplier with supplierFields(BRIGHTSIDE) (fact `supplier`); `doc.create` as sam: creates the Purchase Invoice with invoiceFields of 125.50 USDC from the Supplier (fact `invoice`); `doc.submit` as sam: submits the Purchase Invoice, which posts (fact `invoicePosted`); `doc.create` as sam: creates the Payment Entry with paymentFields from the Capxul Safe account against the invoice (fact `payment`). A journey from it gets it from its template. Facts it adds: `supplier`, `invoice`, `invoicePosted`, `payment`.
- `payment-held`. Made from `payment-drafted`. The Payment Entry is submitted and held for sam's signature; nothing is posted for it yet. Steps: `doc.submit` as sam: submits the Payment Entry, which is held (fact `held`). A journey from it gets it from its template. Facts it adds: `held`.
- `paid`. Made from `payment-held`. sam signed: Brightside was paid 125.50 USDC from the company Safe, the Payment Entry posted and the invoice has nothing outstanding. Steps: `approval.sign` as sam: signs the held payment, which sends it (fact `paidSent`); wait as sam: until report.run's General Ledger shows the Payment Entry. A journey from it gets it from its template. Facts it adds: `paidSent`.
- `with-snapshot`. Made from `paid`. Two snapshots of the world: `m3`, saved as a template, and `draft`, which is not. A snapshot belongs to the world it was saved in, so this world is made by its steps. Steps: `world.snapshot.save` as operator: saves m3 as a template (fact `m3`); `world.snapshot.save` as operator: saves draft (fact `draft`). A journey from it gets it made by its steps. Facts it adds: `m3`, `draft`.
- `restored`. Made from `with-snapshot`. A second private world, made from `m3` by the same operator, which names the first world, `m3` and its record position as its parent. A journey from it runs in the second world. Steps: `world.snapshot.restore` as operator: restores m3 into a new world with a lifetime of 60 minutes (fact `restored`). A journey from it gets it made by its steps. Facts it adds: `restored`.
